derivation: Current session and result/job specifications, checked against implementation before mapping to book.

items.rule: The first complete UTF-8 value reaches stdout unchanged after successful settlement.
An empty value is a result and differs from no result.
Multiline values retain their bytes and receive no added newline.
Unicode values retain their UTF-8 bytes.
Option-looking values remain opaque caller data.
A later nonzero child status does not invalidate a supplied result.
A result over 1 MiB is rejected.
A failed final write or flush is an error and can leave a written prefix.
Publication writes and flushes a temporary regular file before the hard link.
The hard link cannot replace the published value.
Repeated publication succeeds only after validating the existing regular result.
A natural exit without a result fails with status 1.
Natural status 0 without a result still fails.
A readable result alone cannot establish the matching launch outcome.
end-session reads inherited session context without configuration or a target.
Missing session-result context refuses with status 1.
Empty session-result context refuses with status 1.
Stale session-result context refuses with status 1.
The consumer reads through its held directory descriptor.
Readers reject symlinks, FIFOs and other nonregular result entries.
Invalid UTF-8 and oversized result entries cannot become successful results.
Malformed command input fails with status 2.
Malformed owner settings fail before a managed launch.
An unusable exit directory fails with status 2.
A script refusal prevents launch and returns status 3.
A missing or unreadable configuration file prevents launch.
A refused configuration behaviour prevents launch without fallback.
Invalid selection data prevents launch without fallback.
Authority and script failures retain their stage and remedy.
Engine resource limits produce named refusals rather than a managed result.
A missing worker executable prevents selection.
A stale or mismatched protocol, package, build or Rhai identity prevents selection.
Worker spawn and protocol failures prevent launch with status 5.
A valid command is insufficient until actual worker reap and directory removal succeed.
Worker admission requires a successful stop, reap and removal.
Worker status need not be zero when all admission prerequisites hold.
Worker output overflow retains the original conversation report.
Worker teardown uses an absolute 2-second stop bound, including a 1-second grace.
Worker reader draining has its separate bounded wait.
ECHILD or deadline expiry cannot invent a worker reap.
Supervision failure after spawn reports status 5.
Fatal stop or recovery errors retain secondary operation reports.
The whole selection deadline stops evaluation and returns status 124.
A skill-resolution deadline returns status 124.
Cancellation remains distinct from a selection deadline.
Deadline cleanup remains a prerequisite for any subsequent launch.
A selected program that cannot be found fails with status 127.
Another pre-start execution error fails with status 126.
Started records reported spawn and does not prove successful exec.
Failed exec retains the attempted group and terminal lease through recovery.
Recovery reports remain secondary to the original exec error unless cancellation wins.
INT during selection suppresses launch and follows cleanup.
TERM during selection suppresses launch and follows cleanup.
HUP during selection suppresses launch and follows cleanup.
INT during supervision suppresses result success.
TERM during supervision suppresses result success.
HUP during supervision suppresses result success.
Cancellation after result publication still suppresses result success.
The first observed cancellation is retained through settlement.
Front, outcome, late, received and pending observations have an explicit priority.
An already-cancelled skills failure retains its skills stage.
Cancellation preserves reports of cleanup failures and surviving groups.
The CLI restores dispositions and re-raises the signal after required cleanup attempts.
An unknown pending-signal query cannot become a no-cancellation observation.
A signal after the final decision follows restored entry handling.
A result requests 2 seconds of grace before TERM.
TERM receives up to 5 seconds of kill-grace before KILL.
Descendant group cleanup precedes reap on result completion.
Descendant group cleanup precedes reap on natural exit.
Repeated pre-reap group kills preserve the leader identity until actual reap.
Only actual reap emits Reaped.
The post-reap absence query is bounded and sends no numeric group signal.
Error settlement and post-KILL waits have absolute bounds.
Deadline expiry releases ownership without inventing a status.
A surviving group prevents successful result output.
A terminal recovery failure prevents successful result output.
A private-channel cleanup failure prevents successful result output.
The original failure precedes the first outer cleanup failure.
Every secondary cleanup report remains visible.
Without an earlier error, the first cleanup failure precedes a surviving group.
Result stdout is checked and reserved before launch.
Managed stdout is redirected to stderr before spawn.
Partial allocation retains ownership until explicit transfer.
Cleanup checks the private directory identity and preserves a replacement.
A moved owned directory is reported for possible manual removal.
Explicit cleanup disarms destructor retry even when cleanup fails.
Mask, channel, output and final signal settlement join on every outer path.
Interrupted or unconfirmed group outcomes cannot authorise a result.
Each managed session gets a fresh private result channel.
A nested session replaces result context only for its own child.
Six exact legacy and result controls are scrubbed before fresh context is supplied.
Other caller environment variables remain ordinary inherited data.
RAVEL_CONFIG_RUN presence refuses start-session re-entry before configuration selection.
Each harness run uses a separate private channel and captured runner.
A harness result is configuration data and has no managed-session result authority.
Harness output_limit, timed_out, signalled and exited outcomes have explicit precedence.
Missing harness result remains distinct from an empty result.
Harness group or cleanup failure prevents accepted result data.
JSON routing notices and refusal documents go to stderr.
Operation reports remain distinct from the successful opaque stdout result.
confine and runtime-read flags refuse with status 2 after parsing.
Withdrawal refusal precedes settings, skills, worker and channel acquisition.
Separate, combined, equals and positional flag forms follow the same rule.
A token consumed as another flag's value remains caller data.
The harness sandbox supplies the only confinement boundary in Ravel 2.0.0.
An interactive foreground CLI can lend the terminal to its managed group.
A background CLI does not steal the terminal and can lend after later foreground admission.
Noninteractive launches do not lend or recover the terminal.
Captured harness runs do not consume the caller cancellation latch.
The CLI saves terminal modes before the attempted spawn.
Recovery preserves an unrelated terminal holder after normal completion.
Signal death permits broader recovery subject to the documented holder exclusions.
An unknown holder permits recovery only with exclusive authority and a stable recorded group.
Failed exec retains the terminal lease for recovery.
Entry ignored and blocked signal state is captured before runtime setup.
The child reinstates captured entry state independently of host handling.
SIGCHLD handling is repaired before worker creation.
Helper reader threads shield signals from the final join.
Ravel supports one launcher lifetime with exclusive signals and terminal authority.
Same-user tampering is outside result-channel authentication guarantees.
Directory identity comparison and pathname removal are not atomic under same-user races.
Descendants that escape the managed process group are outside cleanup guarantees.
Abrupt CLI death can interrupt cleanup and result delivery.
Bounded harness cancellation does not prove a remote service stopped.
A reader may outlive its bounded wait without proving a reap.
The final signal decision and stdout write are not an atomic transaction.
The private runner is not a supported embedding library.
Native x86-64 Linux remains unqualified despite build, lint and emulation evidence.
Native arm64 macOS and arm64 Linux evidence does not qualify other platforms.
Novice comprehension remains unknown and owner stand-in reads do not establish it.
Real harness flags are supported only by their dated version-specific checks.
Published release rendering does not establish rendering of the current branch.
Inventory coverage does not establish owner Read 2 or whole-book proof.
The private result directory uses --exit-dir when supplied, otherwise TMPDIR.
items.before: Chapter 8 described TMPDIR without the --exit-dir override.
